claims.event: In Yuanhe 2 Emperor Zhang sent Jia Kui to question the calendar specialists.
Under Yongyuan Jia Kui's collected discussion was kept as the basis of later debate.

claims.statement: The Taichu winter solstice at the Ox's beginning is the Ox's middle star. Quarter-remainder matches the observing registers, and schemes that fix the solstice at the Ox's leading edge were discarded.

claims.event: In Jianwu 8 Zhu Fu repeatedly petitioned that the calendar's lunations were wrong.
In Jianwu 8 Xu Shu joined Zhu Fu in asking that the calendar be reformed.
In Jianwu 8 the emperor set calendar revision aside because the realm was newly settled.
In Yongping 5 Yang Cen said the eclipse would fall on the fifteenth, and from the seventh through the eleventh month his predictions matched while the bureau's missed.
In the eleventh month of year 12, read here as Yongping 12, Zhang Sheng and Jing Fang replaced Yang Cen. The bingzi day is not given a Gregorian date, and the month may enter 70.

claims.statement: The moon ought to be eclipsed on the fifteenth; the official calendar misses it.

claims.event: After Yongping 5 Zhang Sheng and others tested the quarter-remainder method against Yang Cen.
On the bingzi day of the eleventh month of year 12, Zhang Sheng succeeded Cen. The era is not restated; it is read as Yongping 12, and the month may enter 70.
Zhang Sheng and Jing Fang had not yet fixed the epoch, so they used quarter-remainder only for quarters and full moons.
Jing Fang was appointed with Zhang Sheng in the eleventh month of year 12.
Bao Ye was among the expectancy holders told to test quarter-remainder against Yang Cen after the Yongping 5 eclipse check.

label.en: expectancy holder of the Grand Astrologer

claims.event: Earlier, in year 9, Dong Meng said the calendar was faulty. The era is not named; before year 12 in this Yongping narrative it is read as Yongping 9.
The discussion of Dong Meng's objection ran to the fourth month of year 10, read as Yongping 10, and no one produced a conclusive case.
In Yuanhe 2 Emperor Zhang questioned the astrologers and called in Bian Xin and Li Fan.
On the jiayin day of the second month of Yuanhe 2 Emperor Zhang issued the calendar edict.
Before a full year of the reform had passed, Emperor Zhang sent Jia Kui to question ten specialists.

claims.statement: The quarter-remainder calendar is adopted to follow Yao and the pattern Confucius praised. The Hetu, the Documents, and the apocrypha are quoted in the edict.

claims.event: In Yuanhe 2 Bian Xin was called to review the calendar and later joined the ten specialists.
Bian Xin still wanted the civil year to open on a long eleventh month, and he noted that the sun stood five degrees short of mid-Ox.
In Yuanhe 2 Li Fan was summoned with Bian Xin and later argued that the long month should come first.
Emperor Zhang's edict recalls Yao at Mount Tai and the pattern of following Yao. No year of Yao is given.

claims.statement: The Yuanhe 2 edict cites Yao as the model for the new calendar.

claims.event: The edict says the clerks still use Deng Ping's Taichu method and that its remainder lies inside a three-hundred-year cycle. His own life is not dated here.

In Yongyuan 14 Li Fan joined Shu and Cheng in replying on the clepsydra statute.
Su Tong, with Li Fan, checked the logs and described the nine-path lunar cycle.
During Xiping Zong Zheng of Liang resubmitted the nine-path theory and the Grand Astrologer found it agreed with the old tables.
During the Xiping check Feng Xun compared his own nine-path adjustments with Zong Zheng's.
Grand Astrologer Yang used Feng Xun's tables for quarters and full moons, and the times could still miss by more than ten degrees.

claims.statement: On the ninth of the third month the officials assembled and Cai Yong debated Guang and Huang. The Zhuanxu method puts Beginning of Spring, a jisi new moon, at five degrees of Encampment.

claims.event: Cai Yong debated right and wrong with Guang and Huang. No year is given in this fragment.
Huang debated with Guang and Cai Yong. No year is given.
Cai Yong quotes the Zhuanxu method: Heaven's origin, first month, jisi dawn new moon, Beginning of Spring, sun and moon at five degrees of Encampment. No year of Zhuanxu's life is given.
Zhao says that without gentlemen there cannot be a state, praises Cai Yong's discussion, and notes that the ministers' verdict and the edict of no prosecution fit the Analects. No year is given.

claims.statement: Without gentlemen, how can there be a state? Cai Yong's discussion shows the hidden workings of heaven. The ministers' verdict was enough, and the edict not to punish also fits the Analects.

claims.event: Zhao says an edict ordered that they not be punished. The sovereign is not named and no year is given.

claims.statement: Liu Hong, courtesy name Fuzhuo, of Mengyin in Taishan, of the Lu kings' house, served in Yanxi, mourned his father, worked with Cai Yong at the Eastern Lodge, and spent more than ten years on the Qianxiang method.

claims.event: During Yanxi Liu Hong answered the Grand Astrologer's summons as a commandant, was made a gentleman and then chief clerk of Changshan, and left office because his father died.

He later edited the calendar record at the Eastern Lodge with Cai Yong, devised the Qianxiang method over more than ten years, concurrently governed Shanyang, and died in office before reaching the capital. The Bowu ji says he was minister of Qucheng. No year is given for the death.
Liu Hong's unnamed father died during Yanxi, and Liu Hong left office to mourn him. The year inside Yanxi is not given.
Zhao praises Cai Yong's discussion. Yuan Shansong says that at the Eastern Lodge Liu Hong and Cai Yong together compiled the calendar record and tested the sky. No year is given.

translationRepairs: The emperor ordered Yang Cen and Pu to make observations and pit their results against the bureau’s calendar.
The emperor ordered Yang Cen to make general observations and pit their results against the bureau’s calendar.
普候 means observe generally. Pu is not a second person.
An edict ordered Cen and Pu to observe and to compete against the official calendar.
An edict ordered Cen to observe generally and to compete against the official calendar.
普 is the adverb generally, not a personal name.
In the eleventh month of Jianwu 12, on bingzi day, Zhang Sheng and Jing Fang were appointed to succeed Cen in timing quarters, full moons, and eclipses.
In the eleventh month of Yongping 12, on bingzi day, Zhang Sheng and Jing Fang were appointed to succeed Cen in timing quarters, full moons, and eclipses.
The Chinese says only 十二年, after Yongping 5. It does not repeat Jianwu. Jianwu 12 would precede Yongping 5.

Before a full cycle of its practice had passed, Emperor Zhang again issued sagely thought, examining it against the classics and prognostications, and sent the Left General of the Gentlemen of the Household Jia Kui to question the calendar specialists [lacuna] Cheng, Li Chong, the Major to the Grand Commandant Liang Wei, the Clerk of the Minister of Education Yan Xu, the Household Grandee for the Heir Apparent Xu Zhen, the ranked commoner of Julu Su Tong, together with Xin, Fan, and others—ten men in all.
左中郎將 is the Left general, not the General for All Purposes (五官中郎將).
The apocryphal Wen yao gou praises High Xin’s ministers defining ritual.
The apocryphal Wen yao gou says: ‘Gaoxin received the mandate; Chong and Li set forth the pattern.’
The Chinese 高辛受命，重黎說文 names Gaoxin, Chong, and Li. The idiomatic text hides Chong and Li behind ministers.
Under Xia’s kings ministers ordered the stellar officers.
Under the Xia sovereign, Kunwu arrayed the spirits.
The Chinese 夏後制德，昆吾列神 names Kunwu. The idiomatic text replaces him with unnamed ministers.
Two years into Han → Wu adopted Taichu with dingchou epoch for 189 years.
After one hundred two years of Han, Emperor Wu adopted Taichu with the dingchou epoch, and it was used for one hundred eighty-nine years.
百有二歲 is one hundred two years, not two, and 百八十九歲 is one hundred eighty-nine years. The literal already says so.
Their totals clash with every standard chronology.
Their totals would miss the Qian zao du and Yuan ming bao, would keep the unicorn capture out of Duke Ai's fourteenth year, and would miss the Mingli xu span from the unicorn to Han.
The Chinese names Duke Ai's fourteenth year and the two apocrypha. The idiomatic sentence drops all three.
Even perfectly tuned calendars did not banish flood or rebellion.

Of old Yao ordered Xi and He to track the sun, moon, and stars; Shun set the seasons and days right; Tang and Wu changed the mandate and clarified the calendar. That was correct, yet they still met flood, drought, and the warning about barbarians and bandits.
The Chinese names Yao, Xi, He, Shun, Tang, and Wu. The idiomatic sentence drops every one of them.
Han has rotated epochs repeatedly since Qin; gengshen is not eternal.

Yuanhe 2 adopted gengshen, and ninety-two years have passed since then. Guang and Huang call it the epoch Qin used to replace Zhou, not seeing that since Qin the Han has changed the epoch three times and has not stayed with gengshen.
The Chinese gives Yuanhe 2 and the ninety-two years. The idiomatic sentence drops both.
The Three Dukes indicted Feng Guang and Chen Huang for disrespect.
Grand Commandant Dan, Minister of Education Kui, and Minister of Works Xun used Cai Yong's opinion to impeach Feng Guang and Chen Huang for disrespect, under the ghost-firewood statute.
The Chinese names Dan, Kui, Xun, and Yong. The idiomatic text collapses them into the Three Dukes.
—second year first month twelfth day—the ranked commoner Zong Gan of Meng memorialized: ‘This month’s sixteenth day the moon ought to eclipse—but the calendar puts it in the second month.’
—twelfth year first month twelfth day—the ranked commoner Zong Gan of Meng memorialized: ‘This month’s sixteenth day the moon ought to eclipse—but the calendar puts it in the second month.’
The preceding unit supplies 十, so the year is 十二年, not 二年.

Clouds obscured two candidate nights in Guanghe 2.

The Chinese names Xiu and Zhang Xun and gives their March-versus-April judgment. The idiomatic sentence drops both men.
Feng Xun and Zong Cheng presented defenses.
Zhang Xun and Zong Cheng presented defenses.

Feng Xun’s observational skill matches eclipses too.
Zhang Xun’s observational skill matches eclipses too.

—Wang Han’s jisi epoch—matches the Kaoling yao yimao anchor and cross-cuts Feng Guang’s jiayin scheme.

The Chinese names 尚書令忠. The idiomatic text drops Zhong.
The Song treatise likewise says “but Deng and the others then let it drop.”
The Song treatise likewise says “Dan and the others then let it drop.”
但等 is Dan and the others. Deng is not in the Chinese.
The phrase "以紺法署施行五十六歲" confirms that 十 is superfluous.
The passage below says Gan's method was applied for fifty-six years. From Yongyuan 2 to Benchu 1 is exactly fifty-six years, so the character 十 is superfluous.
The literal gives the Yongyuan 2 to Benchu 1 count. The idiomatic sentence drops it.
Grand Astrologer Yang submitted, using Xun's method to compare the new and full moons.
太史令揚上 means Yang submitted. The idiomatic sentence does not translate the clause.
Grand Clerk Yang Shang applied Xun’s method to conjunctions and full moons.”
Grand Astrologer Yang submitted Xun’s method to conjunctions and full moons.”
上 is the verb submitted, not part of the name Yang Shang.

Therefore Confucius and Qiuming wrote whenever there was a new moon or an intercalation, correcting the errors and thereby publishing the calendar numbers.
The Chinese names 仲尼 and 丘明. The idiomatic sentence drops both.

The idiomatic sentence does not translate 造三統曆，以修春秋.

The Chinese says Ban Gu called the calendar the most exact. The idiomatic sentence only gestures at irony.
Du Yu sides with conjunction records.
